classification.difficultyReason: Each part is a direct factorial simplification with no new idea. The student unrolls (n+1)! to (n+1)n! and (n-1)! to (n-1)(n-2)!, then cancels the matching factorials. This is the same method as p6-q4, but there are two unrolling decisions in each ratio, and the cancellation across a product of factorials in the numerator and denominator needs tracking. Part b also leaves a non-trivial algebraic fraction, (n+1)/(n-1). There is no combining of fractions, no case analysis and no reframing, so it stays below routine linked multi-step tasks such as p7-q7 and A4.
